newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa tightly mixed by close.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa tightly mixed by close.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures were tightly mixed by the close on Thursday in routine switch activity by locals and trade with the market taking a breather after the recent rally.

"It is taking time off," said one trader. The funds which have built up large long positions were unlikely to initiate new buying unless prices move much higher, origins were well hedged and manufacturers stepped up coverage recently.
"This leaves the locals and the trade jobbing the market," he said.
Benchmark September rose to hit a high of 1,150 stg a tonne before finishing the day at 1,137, the same as previous close. Its intraday low was 1,135.
Prices advanced early in the session but drifted back after failing to trigger key stops. "It pulled back as nothing appeared on the upside," another said.
December was just one stg down at 1,139.
Technically, while the 1,100 stg level basis September remained intact, there was also scope for the market to blip higher to 1,172, analysts said.
The funds might renew their buying at above 1,172 and this would pave the way for a challenge at 1,200.
The downside was seen well supported with a lot of buyers waiting on the dips.
"There could be some (downward) corrective element but it could come back again," said one.
In another story, Barry Callebaut, the company created through a merger between cocoa firms Cacao Barry SA and Callebaut AG, has been approved by a Belgian appeals court.
Barry Callebaut is a unit of Zurich-based Klaus J Jacobs Holding.

The decision will mean that Barry Callebaut will sell a portion of the rights, and the production of Belgium-based Cacao Goemaere to Chocolaterie Jacques, it said. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
